findings.title: 12-hour breach notification window is excessively short
findings.deviation: Clause 4.1 requires notification of a Privacy Event within 12 hours of discovery, which is significantly more restrictive than the 48-72 hour window AtliQ typically seeks.
findings.impact: The subcontractor faces a high risk of technical breach if an incident is not identified and escalated almost immediately upon discovery.
findings.quote: Subcontractor shall report to Business Associate any Privacy Event within twelve (12) hours of discovery.
findings.counterPosition: Align the notification window with the Upstream BAA or provide a minimum of 48 hours for reporting.

findings.title: Blind flow-down of upstream conditions
findings.deviation: Clause 3.1 binds the subcontractor to every restriction and condition in the Upstream BAA without providing the text or a specific list of those obligations.
findings.impact: The subcontractor is bound by unknown contractual terms, increasing the risk of accidental non-compliance.
findings.quote: Subcontractor shall comply with every restriction and condition that applies to Business Associate under the Upstream BAA, including the requirement that Protected Health Information is accessed only from within the United States and only in environments controlled or approved by Harrington.
findings.counterPosition: Attach relevant excerpts or specific conditions of the Upstream BAA as an exhibit to this agreement.

findings.title: Lack of subcontractor termination right
findings.deviation: The agreement duration is tied exclusively to the Upstream BAA with no independent termination for convenience right for the subcontractor.
findings.impact: The subcontractor has no mechanism to exit the agreement independently during the project term.
findings.quote: This Agreement ends when the Upstream BAA ends.
findings.counterPosition: Include a mutual termination for convenience clause providing at least 30 days' notice.

fine.note: The restriction to US-only data access correctly flows down Harrington's security requirements (Clause 3.1).
Requirements for HIPAA safeguards, training, and background checks are standard and appropriate for this subcontractor role (Clause 3.2).
The prohibition on de-identification or secondary use of PHI is standard for a business associate agreement (Clause 3.3).
